item.title: China boycotts Kylian Mbappe after perceived insult to Mao Zedong
item.description: CCTV has reportedly removed advertisements featuring Mbappe, stopped airing soccer matches involving the Frenchman and deleted all posts related to him from its official Weibo account ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: French soccer star Kylian Mbappe is facing mounting backlash in China after comments perceived as insulting Mao Zedong, with state TV blocking his matches, social media freezing his accounts and a slew of companies dropping him as ambassador. CCTV has reportedly removed advertisements featuring Mbappe, stopped airing soccer matches involving the Frenchman and deleted all posts related to him from its official Weibo account. Chinese social media platform Xiaohongshu also froze the footballer’s account after controversy erupted over remarks he made while discussing an internet meme that appeared to depict Mao, modern China’s founding father.  Mbappe’s official accounts on Weibo and Xiaohongshu, which both have around 1 million followers, were marked with notices saying they had been muted for violating regulations.  During a press briefing, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said that any words or actions that offend the Chinese people will inevitably encounter widespread opposition from Chinese society. Consumer brands that hired Mbappe as ambassador — Eastroc Beverage Group Co. and China Mengniu Dairy Co. — saw their stock drop. Shares of Eastroc fell as much as 4.1% in Shanghai, while Mengniu was down around 3% in Hong Kong. Both companies said they are severing ties with him.  Swiss sneaker company On Holding AG also deleted all Mbappe-related posts on its Chinese social media account. The sportswear brand did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its plans regarding its recently signed 10-year partnership with the 2018 World Cup winner. In a video, the footballer was asked which internet meme featuring himself had made him laugh the most. He described one involving a video of a man he said he thought was “a Chinese dictator,” with his own face superimposed on the figure. Mbappe said he frequently used the meme with friends while gaming online, but didn’t identify the person in the meme.  Taiwanese media outlet ETtoday reported that the image depicted Mao. Images circulating online also appeared to show Mbappe’s face superimposed on Mao. Neither Eastroc or Mengniu specified what prompted their decisions or referred to Mao in their statements.  Memes about Mbappe being a dictator have circulated at least since the World Cup this summer. It’s a nickname he’s carried for months and people have superimposed his face on several historical figures, often in military garb.  The episode quickly triggered criticism from nationalist users on Chinese social media, with some accusing Mbappe of insulting China and calling for a boycott. Prominent soccer outlet Dongqiudi said it wouldn’t provide a translation of his remarks as they were “hurtful to China and the Chinese people.” It’s not the first time that online controversies over perceived slights have hurt sponsorships and business ties. The National Basketball Association has worked to rebuild its brand in mainland China after a years-long fallout triggered by a social-media post supporting Hong Kong protesters in 2019 from Daryl Morey, then general manager of the Houston Rockets. Foreign companies including Swedish retailer Hennes & Mauritz AB and sportswear giant Nike Inc. have also faced consumer boycotts over comments on Xinjiang.

item.title: Microsoft India offers voluntary exit with 1 month salary per yr of service
item.description: Eligible employees selected for the programme must decide by December 1, with the package also including health insurance and career transition services ...
item.dc:creator: Aashish Aryan
item.content:encoded: Microsoft will offer employees in India a standard severance package, including one month of base salary for each completed year of service, health insurance and career transition services, as part of its voluntary retirement programme, the company said. Microsoft India employees selected for the voluntary retirement scheme must decide by December 1, the company said. While the company did not share details of the number of employees impacted in India, a spokesperson said Microsoft continues to “invest in India’s talent and technology ecosystem and is backing the country’s AI ambitions with $20.5 billion in committed investment between 2025 and 2029 across cloud and AI infrastructure, skilling and operations”. “We are also on track to fulfil our commitment of equipping 20 million people across India with AI skills by 2030,” the spokesperson said. Earlier on Monday, the company offered a voluntary exit scheme to nearly 60,000 employees globally, or roughly 25 per cent of its 223,000-strong workforce. “This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below,” said Amy Coleman, executive vice-president and chief people officer at Microsoft. The decision to offer the voluntary retirement programme to roughly one-fourth of its workforce comes as companies worldwide look to improve efficiency and shore up revenues with artificial intelligence, leading to layoffs or retirement programmes such as the one Microsoft is offering. In a blog post, Coleman said the voluntary exit offer was an important part of how Microsoft was “creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter”. The voluntary exit programme comes even as Microsoft continues to hire. In a LinkedIn post on Saturday, Coleman said the company welcomed 1,600 new employees between October 19 and 23. “There’s a lot of conversation about what AI will mean for jobs. Some companies see AI as a reason to hire fewer people early in their careers. At Microsoft, we see it differently. Every leader we’ll need in ten years is starting their career somewhere today. We want them starting here,” Coleman said in the post.

item.content:encoded:
Home / Economy / News / No pressure from US to reduce Russian oil imports, says Hardeep Puri

No pressure from US to reduce Russian oil imports, says Hardeep Puri India's imports of West Asian crude oil surged in September, returning to pre-war levels, while its refiners cut back purchases of Russian oil amid stiff competition from China

Hardeep Puri said West Asia oil supplies have been rising as the region is able to ship out more cargoes

Reuters GOA 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 27 2026 | 12:49 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India has faced no pressure from the US to reduce its Russian crude imports, oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Tuesday at an industry event.   "I never felt anything," Puri said when asked if there has been pressure to cut Russian oil imports.   Puri said West Asia oil supplies have been rising as the region is able to ship out more cargoes.   He said India was getting 0.2% of its oil imports from Russia before the Ukraine war, while imports have surged since the war started due to discounts on Russian oil.   India's imports of West Asian crude oil surged in September, returning to pre-war levels, while its refiners cut back purchases of Russian oil amid stiff competition from China, ship-tracking data showed.

The minister said that the purchase of Russian oil is linked to discounts and pricing when compared with other grades. Russian oil imports have been reduced as the refiners are buying more Gulf oil sold at a discount, he added.   "Whatever people say or do, ultimately it is anchored in their self-interest," he said.   The minister also said India is expanding its refining capacity to help meet local demand and export commitments.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Microsoft's Voluntary Exit Offer: Eligibility, benefits, deadline and more
item.description: Microsoft's VEO covers eligible employees at level 70 and below in selected teams across India, the US, the UK and Canada, with individual exit terms and benefits subject to eligibility ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Technology / Tech News / Microsoft's Voluntary Exit Offer: Eligibility, benefits, deadline and more

Microsoft's Voluntary Exit Offer: Eligibility, benefits, deadline and more Microsoft's VEO covers eligible employees at level 70 and below in selected teams across India, the US, the UK and Canada, with individual exit terms and benefits subject to eligibility

Microsoft has around 23,000 employees in India, but the number eligible for the programme remains unclear (Photo: Reuters)

Apexa Rai New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 27 2026 | 10:49 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Microsoft has introduced a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for eligible employees in India, the US, the UK and Canada, giving them the option to leave the company with financial support and career planning resources. The programme, announced on October 26 by Amy Coleman, Microsoft’s executive vice-president and chief people officer, is intended to offer employees "greater flexibility" while allowing teams to adjust their workforce to changing needs. What is Microsoft's VEO? The Voluntary Exit Offer is a time-limited programme that lets eligible employees leave Microsoft voluntarily, with support for the transition. It differs from a compulsory layoff because employees can choose whether to accept the offer.

In her announcement on the official Microsoft blog, Coleman said the initiative builds on the company’s experience with its Voluntary Retirement Programme earlier this year. She said the offer would provide employees considering opportunities outside Microsoft with another option. Who all are eligible? The VEO is available to eligible employees at internal job level 70 and below in participating teams across India, the US, the UK and Canada. However, the offer does not cover every employee at these levels. Eligibility depends on the organisation and its business priorities, customer commitments and workforce requirements.   Microsoft has around 23,000 employees in India, but the number eligible for the programme remains unclear. A PTI report has put the total number of eligible employees globally at approximately 60,000.

Also Read

Employees who qualify are expected to receive an email with a link to their individual offer details. The specific terms, including the benefits available, will depend on the offer communicated to each employee. Why has the company introduced the VEO? Microsoft said the programme is intended to give employees more flexibility in deciding their next career move while helping participating teams respond to changing business needs.   The announcement comes as the technology company continues to invest heavily in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and reassess its workforce requirements.   The initiative follows the company’s Voluntary Retirement Programme earlier this year. Coleman said Microsoft would use the experience gained from that programme to learn from the new offer.

What support do employees get if they accept VEO? Microsoft’s official announcement confirms that eligible employees will receive financial support and career planning resources.   According to a PTI report, the package is understood to resemble a standard severance arrangement, including one month’s base salary for every completed year of service, health insurance, and career transition support. What employees must consider before accepting the VEO? Employees should first establish whether they are eligible and carefully review the terms in their individual offer. The financial package should be assessed against their length of service, current compensation, expected expenses, and the time they may need to find another job.

They should also check the duration and scope of any continued health insurance, the treatment of unvested stock awards, applicable tax implications, and whether any other benefits or contractual obligations are affected.   For Indian employees, the deadline to accept the offer is December 1, The Economic Times reported on Tuesday.
